Arbitrary

AR-bih-trair-ee — ends like 'very scary'; arbitrary rules feel scary because there's no reason behind them. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Arbitrary is based on random choice or personal whim rather than any reason or system.

The coach's decision to bench the team's best player seemed completely arbitrary.

Worked Example

On the first day of class, the teacher assigned seats by pulling names out of a hat. Students asked why they couldn't sit alphabetically or choose their own spots. The teacher shrugged and said there was no particular reason.

A choice made with no reasoned system behind it is arbitrary. Unlike 'unfair,' which implies someone is harmed, an arbitrary decision may hurt no one — it simply lacks any justification.

How Arbitrary Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

random

random: happening without pattern or plan

capricious

capricious: driven by sudden, unpredictable whims

whimsical

whimsical: guided by playful impulse rather than logic

Antonyms

reasoned

reasoned: based on careful logic

systematic

systematic: following a fixed, orderly plan

How Strong Is It? — offhand → arbitrary → tyrannical

offhand vs. arbitrary

offhand vs. arbitrary: An offhand choice is made quickly and casually but may still have some sense behind it, making it weaker than arbitrary, which means there is no reason at all.

tyrannical vs. arbitrary

tyrannical vs. arbitrary: A tyrannical rule is stronger than an arbitrary one — it is not only reasonless but also cruel and oppressive.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — arbitr-

root — arbitr-: judge (Latin)

suffix — -ary

suffix — -ary: relating to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin 'arbiter' meant a judge who decided matters at his own discretion. Something 'relating to the judge's discretion' came to mean decided by one person's whim alone rather than by fixed rules.
